login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: XControl Panel
login.mfaHelp: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.

dashboard.intro: XCP is in early development. Hosting features (accounts, domains, email, DNS) arrive in the next phase.
dashboard.enable2fa: Protect this login with two-factor authentication.

security.title: Login & security
security.forcedPassword: Your password must be changed before you can continue.

password.title: Change password
password.mismatch: The new passwords do not match.
password.changed: Password changed. Your other sessions were signed out.

twofa.title: Two-factor authentication
twofa.scan: Scan this QR code with an authenticator app, or enter the key by hand:
twofa.confirm: Enter a code from the app to finish:
twofa.recoveryHelp: Each code works once if you lose your phone. Store them somewhere safe; they will not be shown again.
twofa.disableHelp: Enter your password to turn off two-factor authentication.

security.mfaRequired: This server requires two-factor sign-in for your login. Set it up below to continue.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.hint: For scripts that call the panel's API (Authorization: Bearer ...). A read token can only read. Tokens cannot change passwords, 2FA or sessions, and cannot confirm a password.
tokens.made: Copy the token now. It is not shown again.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.confirmRevoke: Revoke the token {{name}}? Scripts that use it stop working.

errors.invalid_code: That code is wrong or was already used.
errors.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Please wait and try again.
errors.login_disabled: This login is suspended. Contact your provider.
errors.unauthenticated: Your session has ended. Please sign in again.
errors.csrf_failed: Security check failed. Reload the page and try again.
errors.forbidden: You do not have permission for this.
errors.in_use: It is still in use and cannot be deleted.
errors.domain_taken: Another account already uses this domain.
errors.bad_status: Not possible in the account's current status.
errors.verification_required: Prove that you control this domain first (see below).
errors.limit_reached: Your package allows no more of these.
errors.primary_domain: The primary domain belongs to the account and cannot be removed.
errors.has_dependents: Remove its subdomains and aliases first.
errors.redirect_exists: This domain already has a redirect for that path.
errors.record_conflict: That record does not fit the zone.
errors.record_exists: The zone has this record already.
errors.zone_exists: This server has a DNS zone with that name already.
errors.zone_in_use: The domain's DNS zone also holds records of other domains; remove those domains first.
errors.needs_certificate: The domain needs a valid certificate first.

packages.title: Packages
packages.name: Name
packages.unlimitedHint: Leave a field empty for unlimited.

limits.php_versions_hint: Comma-separated, like 8.2, 8.3. Empty: all installed versions.

featureLists.title: Feature lists
featureLists.help: A feature list decides which parts of the panel accounts on a package can use.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.usernameHint: Lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter. This is also the Linux user name.
accounts.mustChange: Require a new password at next login
accounts.passwordSet: Password changed. The account was signed out everywhere.
accounts.terminateHelp: This deletes the account, its Linux user and all files in its home folder. Type the username to confirm.

domains.title: Domains
domains.noAccount: This login has no hosting account.
domains.name: Domain
domains.docrootHint: Inside your home folder. Leave empty for the suggested one; it is created if missing.

help.addon: Another website with its own folder.
help.sub: A name below one of your domains, such as blog.example.com, with its own folder.
help.alias: Another name that shows the same website as one of your domains.

domains.confirmDelete: Remove {{name}}? Its files stay in your home folder.

verify.intro: Another account on this server uses a domain under the same name. To show that {{name}} is yours, add this DNS record where the domain is managed:
verify.retry: DNS changes can take a few minutes to appear. Then try again.

redirects.title: Redirects
redirects.keepPath: Keep the rest of the path (/old/page goes to destination/page)

web.title: Web settings
web.hint: Per domain. Changes are applied to the web server within a few seconds.
web.errorPagesHint: The address of a page on this site (like /errors/404.html) shown instead of the server's own page. Leave empty for the default.
web.hotlinkOn: Refuse other sites that embed these files
web.hotlinkSites: Other sites that may embed them
web.hotlinkEmpty: Allow requests without a referrer (direct visits)
web.blocked: Blocked addresses (one per line, addresses or networks)
web.cache: Browser caching: file types and days, one rule per line

dns.title: DNS zones
dns.empty: No zones yet. Every domain gets one.
dns.name: Name
dns.managedHint: Made for a domain and removed with it. You can still change it.
dns.nameserversHint: This zone is served by {{names}}. Set these name servers at your domain's registrar.
dns.notServing: The DNS server does not have this zone yet. It is added automatically once the DNS server runs (checked every 5 minutes).
dns.valueHint: For a host name: @ is the zone, one word is in the zone (mail), a name with dots is complete.
dns.txtHint: Plain text; long text is split for DNS automatically.
dns.advanced: Advanced: type the whole value myself

mail.title: Email routing
mail.help: Who receives the mail for this domain. The mail server of this panel uses it.

settings.title: DNS settings
settings.nameserversHelp: Every zone lists these as its NS records. If they are names under your own domain, register them with glue IPs at the registrar.
settings.noNameservers: None set yet: each zone names ns1 and ns2 of its own domain, which only works if those exist. Enter your name servers here.
settings.addressesHelp: The public addresses new zones point to. This server's interfaces have: {{ips}} (behind NAT, enter the public address).
settings.templateHelp: The records of every new domain's zone. Use {domain}, {ip4} and {ip6}; records that need a missing address are left out.

ssl.title: SSL/TLS
ssl.forceHttps: Force HTTPS (visitors over HTTP are sent to HTTPS)
ssl.confirmRemove: Remove the certificate of {{name}}? HTTPS stops until AutoSSL issues a new one.
ssl.noCertificates: No certificates yet. AutoSSL issues them for domains that point to this server.
ssl.enabled: AutoSSL is on (runs daily, renews 30 days before expiry)
ssl.hostnameHint: Its certificate is used by the panel. No account can add this name.
ssl.eabKeyId: EAB key ID (if the CA needs one)
ssl.caBundle: CA certificate of the ACME server (only for a private CA)

server.jobsFailed: {{n}} failed jobs in the last 24 hours
server.setupHint: The server setup is not finished.
server.sessionsHint: Signing a session out ends it at once; the person can sign in again with their password. To lock a person out, suspend the account or change the password.

settings.title: Server settings
settings.setupHint: The server's name, time zone, contact address and DNS defaults. You can change them any time.
settings.hostnameHint: Changing the host name changes the system, /etc/hosts and the mail server's name. The panel keeps its current certificate until AutoSSL issues one for the new name.

names.security_password_classes: Character types a password must mix

hints.php_default_version: Used by accounts that did not choose a PHP version. Empty: the newest installed.
hints.php_upload_max_mb: The largest file a PHP page can receive (upload_max_filesize; post_max_size is this plus 8). Applied to every account.
hints.auth_session_idle_minutes: Panel users are signed out after this long without using the panel.
hints.auth_session_max_hours: Panel sessions end after this long, however active.
hints.updates_channel: stable: finished releases only; beta: pre-releases too.
hints.updates_window_hour: When updates may be installed, in server time. Installing from the panel is not available yet; this is kept for it.
hints.auth_require_2fa: none; admins; resellers (admins and resellers); all. Logins that must and have not set it up can only reach the page to do so.
hints.ssh_password_auth: Off allows keys only. Refused while no login has an authorized SSH key, because that would lock everyone out.
hints.ssh_root_login: yes; prohibit-password (keys only); no. Checked with sshd -t before it is applied.
hints.security_password_min_length: For every password made or changed in the panel (logins, mailboxes, FTP, databases). Not below 10.
hints.security_password_classes: 0 to 4 of: lower case, upper case, digits, other characters. Existing passwords stay until changed.

settings.updatesHint: Looks for a newer XCP release on GitHub, in the channel set above. Installing updates from the panel is not available yet.
settings.rebuildHint: Applies every account, DNS zone and the mail server's settings again, from the panel's database. Use it after restoring files or when the server drifted.
settings.confirmRebuild: Apply everything again? This can take a while on a big server.
settings.rebuilding: Queued: {{accounts}} account(s) and {{zones}} DNS zone(s), and the mail settings.
settings.rebootHint: Restarts the server in a few seconds. Graceful stops services in order; forced does not and can lose data. Websites and mail are down for a minute or two.
settings.rebooting: The server is restarting. The panel comes back in a minute or two.

backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: A backup holds your files (mail included), your databases and your account's settings. Download it to keep a copy elsewhere. You can keep {{max}} of your own; the server's scheduled backups come on top.
backups.scheduledNote: The server also backs up on a schedule (at {{hour}}:00 server time) and keeps {{keep}} per account.
backups.hint: A backup file contains your account's secrets (password hashes, keys): keep it private.
backups.removedHint: When an account is removed its backups stay here. Restoring one creates the account again with its files, databases, mail, DNS and certificates.
backups.confirmRestore: Create the account {{name}} again from this backup?
backups.scheduleHint: Times are the server's. Every active account is backed up; the oldest scheduled backups beyond "keep" are deleted.
backups.enabled: Back up every account on a schedule

stats.title: Usage and logs
stats.hint: Counted from the web, mail and FTP logs, about a minute behind; days are in UTC.

cron.title: Cron jobs
cron.intro: Cron jobs run a command on a schedule, as your account's user from your home folder. Times are the server's ({{zone}}).
cron.monthly: On the 1st of every month at 3:00
cron.commandHint: The command runs with /bin/sh. A run that is still going when the next one is due is not started twice; runs stop after 12 hours.
cron.emailPlaceholder: empty: keep the output here only

ftp.title: FTP
ftp.intro: FTP logins let you, or someone you give one to, upload files with an FTP program such as FileZilla. Each login sees only its folder of your home.
ftp.securityHint: Use "FTP over TLS (explicit)" in your FTP program, so the password is not sent in the clear.
ftp.folderHint: The login cannot leave its folder. A missing folder is created.
ftp.shownOnce: Write this down: the password is not shown again.
ftp.confirmDelete: Delete the FTP login {{login}}? Its files stay.

databases.title: Databases
databases.intro: Database and user names start with {{prefix}}. Applications on this server connect to {{host}}.
databases.wizardHint: Creates a database and a user with all privileges on it, for an application such as WordPress.
databases.connectionInfo: Connection details (the password is shown only now):
databases.name: Name
databases.confirmDelete: Delete the database {{name}} with all its data? This cannot be undone.
databases.rootHint: Root on this server always reaches MariaDB through its socket. A root password is for your own tools.

email.title: Email
email.name: name
email.confirmDelete: Delete the mailbox {{name}}? Its mail stays in the account's files.
email.targets: Addresses to forward to, separated by commas
email.aliasOf: mail goes to the same address at {{name}}
email.catchAll: Mail to unknown addresses goes to
email.repaired: The records were written into the domain's DNS zone.
email.nothingToRepair: The zone has the records already. If the check still fails, DNS may need time to update.
email.clientsHint: Log in with the full email address and its password.
email.hostnameHint: Used to greet other mail servers; should match the reverse DNS (PTR) of the server's address.
email.relayHint: Send all outgoing mail through this server; empty delivers directly.
email.heloChecks: Refuse senders without a valid HELO name
email.scriptHint: A path in your home folder. The script runs as your account with the sender and recipient as arguments and gets the message on its input; it must be executable.
email.subject: Subject
email.everyDays: Reply to a sender once in (days)

queue.title: Mail queue
queue.hint: Mail Postfix has not delivered yet, and why. Deferred mail is tried again by itself; flush tries it now. Deleting loses the message.
queue.confirmDeleteAll: Delete every deferred message for good?

files.title: Files
files.name: Name
files.dropHint: Drop files here to upload them to this folder.
files.searchHint: Part of a file or folder name
files.moreResults: There are more; search more precisely.
files.partial: The folder has too many files to count them all; sizes are partial.

firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.hint: Your address is {{ip}}; the panel listens on port {{port}}. A change that would shut you out puts your address on the allow list.
firewall.policyOpen: Open: let in everything not refused
firewall.policyClosed: Closed: let in only the open ports
firewall.ports: Open ports (one per line, e.g. 25/tcp # mail)
firewall.allow: Always allowed (address or network per line)
firewall.deny: Always refused (address or network per line)
firewall.restrict: Restrict a service to some networks
firewall.restrictHint: Leave empty to let everyone reach it. Addresses and networks, separated by commas.
firewall.bruteEnabled: Ban addresses that fail to sign in too often
firewall.permanentAfter: Ban for good after this many bans (0: never)
firewall.addedYourIp: Your address {{ip}} was added to the allow list so you cannot lock yourself out.
firewall.saved: Saved. The rules are being applied.
